items.quote: In H1 FY 2025, we generated a strong operational cash flow amounting to INR 792.4 million, with free cash flow reaching INR 663.2 million.

items.statement: Free cash flow was approximately INR 453 crores with a net release of about INR 23 crores in working capital in the first half of the fiscal year.
items.quote: Our free cash flow amounted to approximately INR 453 crores with a net release of about INR 23 crores in working capital in the first half of this fiscal, and we remain focused on sustaining this efficiency in cash collections as well as conversion rates.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash from operating activities was INR340 crores in H1 FY25, up from INR303 crores in H1 FY24.
items.quote: we have generated net cash from operating activities for th e first half to the tune of almost INR340 crores, which last year for the same first half was INR303 crores

items.statement: Standalone cash flow from operating activities was INR198 crores in Q2 FY25.
items.quote: if I just speak about the current quarter, the overall for th e stand-alone cash flow generated from operating activities is INR198 crores

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced by INR57 crores in Q2 FY25 despite weak revenue and earnings.
items.quote: we have reduced the debt by almost close to INR57 crores during the quarter, despite this being a weak quarter in terms of overall revenue and earnings.

items.statement: Maintenance capex for H1 FY25 was INR94 crores, similar to last year.
items.quote: our over all investment into maintenance capex, etcetera, is almost same as last year at this time for the first half, close to about INR94 crores

items.statement: Rivulis is a competitor in India, a customer for exports, and Jain Irrigation holds a stake in Rivulis' parent company from a past deal.
items.quote: We continue to hold the stake into the company. The y continue to buy products from us. We continue to compete with them in India. Those are t he facts. They are all transparent. They are all arm's length. They are all market based

items.statement: Jain Irrigation will not invest new money from the parent into the food processing subsidiary; expects subsidiary to improve its balance sheet on its own.
items.quote: No. We would not be investing new money out of the parent into the subsidiary. I think we would expect subsidiary on its own to improve its balance sheet.

items.statement: Receivable days decreased to 85 days as of September 30, 2024 from 100 days a year earlier
items.quote: The Company has been seeing that the receivable days have been coming down, as we saw that these receivable days are at 85 days as of 30th September, '24, compared to 100 days in the similar period last year.
